title: Correction-order improvement for nonlinear correctors
summary: Determine whether a nonlinear corrector can strictly exceed the source's best known correction-order constructions for fixed $(n,m)$.

formal_statement.body: Decide whether there exists an admissible pair $(n,m)$ and a nonlinear $(n,m)$-function that is an $(n,m,t)$-corrector with correction order $t$ strictly larger than every correction order achieved by the source's previously known nonlinear construction methods for that pair; if not, prove those benchmark bounds optimal for all admissible $(n,m)$.

scope.domain: Nonlinear corrector construction for cryptographic post-processing of true random-number generators
assumptions: The corrector and correction-order definitions are those of the TIT source
The benchmark is the source's previously known construction families
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result exhibits a strict correction-order improvement over the source benchmark or proves the benchmark universally optimal.

progress.summary: The source's second open problem asks for a nonlinear $(n,m)$ function with correction order better than known constructions.
